units.source_text: 前文所述的伊豫介，在桐壶帝驾崩后之次年，改官常陆介，赴常陆国就任。

en.t: The Iyo Assistant Governor mentioned earlier was transferred the year after Emperor Kiritsubo's death to become Assistant Governor of Hitachi, and went there to take up his post.

units.source_text: 他的夫人，即咏“帚木”之诗的空蝉，随夫前往任地。

en.t: His wife, Utsusemi, who had composed the poem about the broom tree, accompanied her husband to his place of office.

units.source_text: 这空蝉住在常陆，遥闻源氏公子流放须磨，心中也不免偷偷地惋惜。

en.t: While living in Hitachi, Utsusemi heard from afar that Prince Genji had been exiled to Suma, and in her heart she could not help secretly grieving for him.
She wished to send word of her longing, but sadly had no suitable way to do so.

units.source_text: 从筑波山到京都，并非没有便人，但总觉得不当稳便。

en.t: It was not that there were no messengers traveling from Mount Tsukuba to Kyoto, but it never seemed proper or safe enough.

units.source_text: 因此多年以来，一点消息也不通。

en.t: For that reason, for many years not a single message passed between them.

units.source_text: 源氏公子谪居须磨，原无定期。

en.t: Prince Genji's exile at Suma had no fixed term from the beginning.

units.source_text: 后来忽然获赦，仍返京都。

en.t: Later, however, he was suddenly pardoned and returned once more to Kyoto.

units.source_text: 次年秋，常陆介也任满返京了。

en.t: In the autumn of the following year, the Assistant Governor of Hitachi also completed his term and returned to the capital.

units.source_text: 他率领眷属在逢坂入关那一天，正值源氏公子赴石山寺还愿。

en.t: On the day he led his household through the barrier at Osaka, Prince Genji happened to be going to Ishiyama Temple to fulfill a vow of thanks.

units.source_text: 他的儿子纪伊守等从京中到关上来迎接他，将此消息报告了他。

en.t: His son, the Governor of Kii, and others came from the capital to meet him at the barrier and reported this news to him.

units.source_text: 常陆守闻讯，心念在路上相逢，未免嘈杂混乱，因此在天色未晓之前就赶早动身。

en.t: When the Governor of Hitachi heard it, he thought that meeting Genji on the road would inevitably cause noise and confusion, so he set out early before dawn.

units.source_text: 然而女眷所乘车子太多，迤逦前行，不觉已日高三丈了。

en.t: Yet there were so many carriages carrying the women of the household that the procession moved slowly along, and before they knew it the sun was already high in the sky.
